mcat_description.short: Mobile containers are purpose-built or modified steel container structures — typically based on ISO 20ft or 40ft frames — sold as portable shops, offices, site cabins, storage units, or residential units that can be relocated by crane or truck.
mcat_description.long: Mobile containers in the Indian B2B market are prefabricated steel structures built on ISO shipping container frames (predominantly 20ft × 8ft and 40ft × 8ft) that are fitted out for commercial, industrial, or residential use and designed for relocation. They are manufactured from mild steel or corten steel with insulated wall panels (PUF, EPS, or rock wool sandwich panels), pre-installed electrical wiring, windows, and doors, and are customised to buyer specifications for use as retail shops, food stalls, site offices, labour camps, guard cabins, or portable homes. Standard certifications include ISO/CSC plate and TPI inspection; surface treatment typically involves epoxy zinc-rich primer with synthetic enamel or PU topcoat. The Indian market is served by a mix of fabricators who modify used ISO containers and manufacturers who build purpose-built container-form structures from scratch.

market_context: In the Indian market, 'Mobile Containers' commercially refers to prefabricated or modified steel container structures — predominantly based on 20ft × 8ft ISO frames — that are fitted out and sold for use as portable shops, offices, site cabins, storage units, or residential dwellings. The dominant buyer-facing product is the 'container shop' (also called container dukan or kirana container), driven by demand from small business owners and food & beverage operators seeking low-cost, relocatable commercial premises. Standard sizes in the Indian market are 20ft × 8ft × 8'6" (standard height) and 40ft × 8ft × 8'6"/9'6" (high cube), with custom sizes from 4ft × 4ft up to 60ft × 15ft also available from Indian fabricators. Materials are predominantly mild steel (MS) or corten steel with PUF/EPS/rock wool insulated sandwich panel walls; surface treatment is typically epoxy zinc-rich primer with synthetic enamel or PU topcoat. Certifications relevant to the Indian market include ISO/CSC plate (for containers meeting international container standards) and TPI (Third Party Inspection). The Indian supplier base includes both fabricators who modify used ISO shipping containers and manufacturers who build purpose-built container-form structures from scratch — these two supply types serve overlapping but distinct buyer needs. Key manufacturing hubs include Delhi NCR, Ahmedabad, Thane/Mumbai, Chennai, and Bengaluru. The MCAT name creates a contamination risk: bare ISO shipping containers for logistics/freight (a different buyer and taxonomy destination) frequently appear alongside fitted container structures in search results and on-platform listings.
